statement: The signed Euler count of real lines on a generic real hypersurface of degree 2n−3 in RP^n equals (2n−3)!!. More generally, if the induced symmetric-power tautological-bundle section has only isolated real zeros, the sum of the absolute values of their local Euler indices is at least (2n−3)!!.

answer.text: The signed Euler count of real lines on a generic real hypersurface of degree 2n−3 in RP^n equals (2n−3)!!. answer.display: Signed Euler count: (2n−3)!!; sum of absolute local Euler indices ≥(2n−3)!!
answer.qualification: The signed Euler count and local Euler-index weighting are the claims recorded here. At regular zeros the absolute indices are one; at nonregular zeros they are distinct from the algebraic multiplicities of Okonek–Teleman.

scope: Generic real degree 2n−3 hypersurfaces in RP^n, where catalogue n is the ambient projective dimension. For ordinary real-line counts, the associated section is transverse; the broader isolated-line statement weights each line by the absolute value of its local Euler index.
notes: Let n_source be the paper’s variable and n_catalogue the catalogue’s ambient dimension. The conversion is n_source = n_catalogue − 1, so n_source + 1 = n_catalogue and 2n_source − 1 = 2n_catalogue − 3. The lower bound need not be sharp. Local Euler-index multiplicities differ from the algebraic multiplicities of Okonek–Teleman.
